conviction_note: No unpriced company-level number decides this print: the quarter (peak Ford Amphitheater season) has a thin one-analyst bar of ~$5.5-5.6M revenue, the post-quarter financing package is already public in 8-Ks, and the open questions the release must answer (C-PACE status, Sunset cost overrun, Hipgnosis definitive docs) lean mildly negative while 12 days-to-cover and director buying lean the other way; abs_move 7 on 96% realised vol and a history with -40/-21 tails, p_up 45 because this name has fallen on 5 of its last 8 prints, giving -0.7, close to the findings' sum of -0.6.
bar: Q3 FY2026 (quarter ended 2026-09-30) revenue consensus $5.61M (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/VENU/estimates; https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/venu/earnings) / $5.5M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/VENU/earnings-forecasts); EPS -$0.29 to -$0.30. Stockalarm says one analyst ($6M) (https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/VENU/analysts). No company guidance for Q3 or FY (Q2 release, https://finviz.com/news/381690/venu-holding-corporation-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial-results). Bar is two-source-agreeing but rests on ~1 analyst, so sizes are capped small. Comparable: Q3 2025 reported revenue ~$5.38M vs $7.43M expected (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2025-11-14-venu-holding-co-stock/).
positioning_check: Short interest 4,824,107 shares at FINRA settlement 2026-10-30, ~8.6% of 56.2M shares outstanding, 12.2 days to cover, down 264,531 from the prior period; mid-October peak ~5.09M (https://equibles.com/stocks/venu/shortinterest, read 2026-11-13). Options: chain unusable (total OI 16, ATM not two-sided), no skew, no implied move; baseline falls back to median historical reaction 3.85%. Tape: spot $1.21, -6.9% over 5d, +4.3% over 20d, -89% from 52w high, 7% above 52w low, realised vol 96% annualised, avg volume ~350k shares (~$0.4M/day). 12 DTC on a $70M cap is a crowded short relative to liquidity, which shrinks every negative here.

findings.finding: After quarter-end VENU closed a funding package that replaces the bridges: $60M McKinney land sale-leaseback to STORE Capital (closed 2026-10-20; used partly to repay the $20M Ryan bridge in full), $7.5M Centennial sale-leaseback (2026-10-16), Aramark's $5.01M second preferred tranche (2026-10-15), and the YA $25M debenture cut to $12.5M by applying the holdback with no premium, installments now paid in cash ($2.875M paid 2026-10-14); the Q3 10-Q subsequent-events note and liquidity/going-concern assessment will reflect this against June 30 cash of only $16.3M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Financing has driven this stock's biggest print reaction: 2026-01-27 -40.2% when a $75M equity offering was launched alongside Q4 prelims (later terminated). Non-dilutive financing has not had a print to test; the stock fell from ~$1.52 (late Sept) to $1.21 despite these 8-Ks.
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-Ks are public, so the facts are known; what is not yet visible is the consolidated liquidity picture (cash at Sep 30, remaining construction commitments, going-concern language) that the 10-Q puts in one place. If the market had priced a funded runway, the stock would not be 7% above its 52-week low with 12 days-to-cover of shorts betting on dilution. What the money buys: completion of two venues with $285M of cumulative FireSuite sales (Q2 call), i.e. it funds contracted demand, not losses alone.
findings.independence: Second document: the 2026-10-19 8-K on the debenture reduction and Aramark tranche (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1770501/000149315226047620/form8-k.htm). Equibles notes the Aug 10-Q already said going-concern doubt was alleviated (https://equibles.com/stocks/venu/shortinterest). Counter: the STORE ground lease carries $5.7M/yr initial rent on $60M (~9.5%), an expensive mid-term financing.

findings.finding: Sunset Amphitheater (McKinney) cost has risen to about $334M against the ~$220M in the original development agreement (design changes: premium seating in the bowl, climate control, show tech), per city officials on 2026-10-07; the amended 380 agreement itself still references a $220M anticipated budget, so the Q3 10-Q commitments/capex disclosure is where the extra ~$114M of funding need shows up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print isolated a capex overrun; H1 2026 capex was $132.9M against $16.3M ending cash, and the stock has fallen ~40% since the Q2 print.
findings.why_not_priced: A local-news figure from a city council meeting, not in any company release or wire copy; the company's own releases say construction 'continues to move rapidly'. If priced, the call would already be framed around how the gap is funded; previews (there are almost none) carry only EPS/revenue.
findings.independence: The 2026-10-26 8-K cites $220M as total anticipated development budget for the tax-protest clause (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1770501/000149315226048581/form8-k.htm), confirming the original figure the overrun is measured against. Partly offset by finding 1 (the STORE money funds completion).

findings.finding: The >$150M CBRE-arranged C-PACE financing that the company said on 2026-07-09 would close 'in the coming weeks' and on 2026-08-03 'in the third quarter of 2026' has not been announced as closed by 2026-11-13; meanwhile McKinney was refinanced through a sale-leaseback instead and Regent Bank Amphitheater (Broken Arrow) moved from 'fall 2026' / 'roughly 90 days' (Q2 call) to a December winter preview with the full season in summer 2027. The Q3 release/call must state C-PACE status.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Analyst Paul Yankey (Gazette, 2026-08-30) framed C-PACE closing as the key positive; the stock went from $2.02 then to $1.21 with no closing announced.
findings.why_not_priced: Absence of a closing is visible only by noticing nothing was filed; no 8-K item 1.01/2.03 for a C-PACE loan appears in EDGAR through 2026-10-26. A slide from $2.02 to $1.21 may already embed some of it; a confirmed closing on the call would be a positive surprise, a 'no longer pursuing' a negative one, so the range is wide on both sides.
findings.independence: Bridge-to-C-PACE language in the Aug 3 release (https://finviz.com/news/375938/venu-secures-25-million-debt-financing-fueling-regent-bank-amphitheaters-path-to-fall-2026-opening); Regent Bank opening shifted to December (https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260923854498/en/Regent-Bank-Amphitheater-Opens-Its-Doors-This-December-Marking-VENUs-Entry-into-the-Oklahoma-Live-Entertainment-Market); EDGAR 8-K list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001770501&type=8-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=10). Caveat: the debenture holdback was returned because the company 'no longer needed' it, which could mean other funding arrived.

findings.finding: Directors bought in the open market into the decline: Thomas Finke bought 54,644 shares at $1.949 on 2026-08-25 and 50,000 at $1.518 on 2026-09-29, taking his direct holding from 129,605 to 379,605 across an Aug-Sep run of ~17 Form 4 filings; Stephen Cominsky bought 3,234 at $1.70 on 2026-09-17.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Insider buying in Feb-Mar 2026 (CEO Roth at $5.23 and $4.00) did not stop the slide; no print-day evidence that insider buying pays here.
findings.why_not_priced: Public Form 4s, so known; a director adding ~$400k+ ahead of the Q3 close is a weak signal that the quarter/financing was not deteriorating. If the market weighted it, short interest would not sit at 12 days-to-cover.
findings.independence: Second Finke Form 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1770501/000149315226045391/0001493152-26-045391.txt) and Cominsky (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1770501/000149315226043617/0001493152-26-043617.txt); same insider class, so one signal.

findings.finding: Chairman/CEO J.W. Roth's holding company received a 5-year warrant for 5,000,000 shares at $1.20 (about 8.5% of the 58.9M shares outstanding) on 2026-10-20 as consideration for personally guaranteeing the STORE ground lease, plus a guarantee fee, indemnity and security; the Q3 10-Q will carry it as a subsequent event and in fully diluted share counts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print on a related-party grant; Pomerantz investigation headlines followed the January episode.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in an 8-K item 3.02 and a Form 4, so mostly priced; residual is governance optics if the call is asked about it. Struck at the money ($1.20) with spot at $1.21.
findings.independence: Same transaction in the 2026-10-26 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1770501/000149315226048581/form8-k.htm); one fact.

findings.finding: Reported quarter: Q3 is the Ford Amphitheater peak season, but in H1 2026 event center ticket and fee revenue fell to $1.90M from $2.42M (-21.5%; Q2 alone ~$1.0M, -27%), total revenue grew only 7%, and Q3 2025 revenue (~$5.38M) missed its $7.43M bar and the stock fell 21.5%; against a ~$5.5-5.6M one-analyst bar a modest miss is more likely than a beat, with net loss guided to keep widening.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 revenue miss: -21.45% (2025-11-17); Q2 2026 in-line revenue, EPS -$0.30 vs -$0.29: +4.59% close-to-close but -3.4% to $1.98 per Simply Wall St; Q1 2026 -3.11%.
findings.why_not_priced: No independent attendance or gross data for the 2026 Ford season exists in the public record beyond two premium sellouts (June 16 release); the bar is one analyst, so a revenue line that keeps the H1 ticket-fee decline would not have been modelled by anyone else. Losses are guided to widen, so EPS is not the line.
findings.independence: Premium sellouts for two June shows (https://www.chartmill.com/news/external/45431/bizwire-2026-6-16-venus-ford-amphitheater-reports-exceptional-premium-seating-performance-across-back-to-back-shows) point the other way; Q3 2025 miss (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2025-11-14-venu-holding-co-stock/).

findings.finding: The 2026-08-16 binding term sheet with Merck Mercuriadis (Hipgnosis Artist Holdings / Welcome to the Machine) — $3.25M paid for 50%, unwinding if definitive documents are not signed within 90 days (about 2026-11-14), and a $51.75M contribution obligation within 90 days if a $200M+ 'Funding' closes — hits its deadline the weekend before the print, so the release or call should say whether it was signed, extended or unwound.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; the deal was announced after the Q2 print and never discussed on a call.
findings.why_not_priced: Buried in an 8-K item 1.01 with no wire coverage found; a cash-constrained developer committing to a possible $51.75M content investment is a capital-allocation question nobody has asked publicly. Small because the obligation is contingent on a third-party $200M funding.

findings.finding: Short interest of 4.82M shares (8.6% of shares outstanding) at 12.2 days to cover on ~$0.4M/day of turnover (FINRA 2026-10-30), with the stock 7% above its 52-week low, means a release that removes the dilution fear (funded runway, C-PACE closed) can force covering in a thin tape over the one-session window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Stock rose after the January offering was terminated (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/2607803745), the one observed relief event.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price-setter here rather than a missed fact; the asymmetry is that the negatives above are what shorts are already positioned for, so they are partly in the price, while a positive surprise meets 12 days of cover.
findings.independence: Baseline avg volume 349,787 shares and spot $1.21 confirm the thin tape (sealed baseline).

baseline_tension: No skew or implied move to cut against; the evidence leans mildly negative in line with the -89% drawdown and the 5-of-8 down print history, while the 12 days-to-cover short and director buying argue the negatives are largely positioned for.
lessons_applied: Lesson 4 (financing is a question): asked what the post-quarter money buys (completion of venues with $285M of FireSuite sales); kept the funding package positive at +1.0 and shrank the cost-overrun negative from -1.0 to -0.7 because finding 1 funds part of the gap.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): 12.2 days to cover cut the C-PACE negative from -1.0 to -0.8.
Lesson 6 (bar on ~one analyst): reported-quarter finding left capped at -0.5; p_up kept near 50.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): name has sold 5 of 8 prints; p_up held at 45, abs_move unchanged at 7.
Left standing: insider buying, chairman warrant, Hipgnosis deadline and positioning findings unchanged.
